review.title: Profile model
review.acceptance: Profiles are modelled above authentication rather than inside the auth library, with the active profile carried alongside the session rather than inside the identity record; profile scoping is present in the first migration rather than retrofitted, because that is the part that is expensive to reverse; profiles can be created and selected with authorization tests

integration.evidence: THE MODEL WAS EXERCISED AGAINST A REAL DATABASE, NOT RECONCILED OR INFERRED. PostgreSQL 16.15 (Ubuntu 16.15-0ubuntu0.24.04.1), cluster 16/main started in this container; a dedicated role liberty_pl0402 and its own database were created rather than using the superuser, following PL-0405's precedent. psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f packages/persistence/migrations/0000_profile_scoped_identity.sql against an EMPTY database, exit 0, 8 tables: account, active_profile_selection, playback_progress, profile, session, user, verification, watchlist_entry. THE SCHEMA ANSWERS THE FIRST THREE ACCEPTANCE CLAUSES MECHANICALLY, queried from information_schema rather than read off the migration text. Profiles are above authentication: no column matching %profile% exists on user, session, account or verification -- the identity record does not carry one. The active profile is beside the session: active_profile_selection is its own table whose PRIMARY KEY is session_id, with foreign keys to session.id and user.id AND a COMPOSITE foreign key (profile_id, user_id) to profile (id, user_id). Scoping is in the FIRST migration rather than retrofitted: this is 0000, and playback_progress and watchlist_entry both carry a profile_id foreign key to profile in it. THE BEHAVIOURAL HALF DRIVES THE SHIPPED FUNCTIONS, not a reimplementation: createProfile, loadProfileOwnership, listProfilesForAccount, authorizeProfileSelection, selectActiveProfile, loadActiveProfileId, resolveLibertySession and archiveProfile, over a drizzle handle from the package's own createDatabase. Only the auth rows were seeded directly, because authentication is PL-0405's delivery rather than this task's. 13 assertions passed. Creation: the row is readable back from PostgreSQL; listProfilesForAccount returns exactly the account's own profile; a duplicate display name is refused as display_name_already_used BY THE REAL UNIQUE CONSTRAINT rather than by a pre-check. Selection: the grant is accepted, loadActiveProfileId reads it back out of active_profile_selection, and resolveLibertySession carries it beside the session. Archive: accepted under the owner's own scope. AUTHORIZATION IS PROVEN THREE WAYS AND THE FIRST ONE WAS A HARNESS FAILURE THAT TURNED INTO EVIDENCE. A SCOPE CANNOT BE MINTED FROM OUTSIDE @liberty/auth: the harness's first draft called issueProfileScope and failed at runtime with 'issueProfileScope is not a function', because the barrel exports it by name and deliberately omits that one while the brand stays module-private. That is PL-0405's forgery fix holding against a real attempt rather than a test double. The only route to a scope is authorizeProfileSelection on ownership read from the database. Second, that decision REFUSES another account's profile as profile_not_owned_by_account, so no scope is issued at all. Third, when the owner's genuine scope is replayed under the attacker's session, selectActiveProfile independently refuses it as scope_not_granted_to_this_session and nothing is written for that session. AND THE DATABASE REFUSES IT TOO, WHICH IS THE PART AN APPLICATION TEST CANNOT SHOW: inserting the selection row directly, bypassing every application check, fails with SQLSTATE 23503 on active_profile_selection_profile_owner_fk -- the composite (profile_id, user_id) foreign key. Cross-profile access is therefore refused by construction in the schema, not only by convention in the code. THREE HARNESS DEFECTS WERE FOUND AND CORRECTED BEFORE ANY CONCLUSION WAS DRAWN, and they are reported because the first one nearly became a false accusation. (1) The harness omitted the required instant on CreateProfileInput, so createdAt was undefined and PostgreSQL refused the insert with 23502. The first reading was 'createProfile is broken against a real database'; the code was correct and the harness was not. (2) It tried to mint a scope directly, which is the forgery route PL-0405 closed. (3) It passed a LibertySession where loadActiveProfileId takes an AccountIdentity, so the lookup silently matched nothing and returned null. Each was diagnosed against the source before being called a defect. THE HARNESS IS NOT COMMITTED: it ran from a scratch file that was deleted, and git status is clean. It is evidence of an execution, not a deliverable, and PL-0402's allowedPaths do not include a home for it. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: nothing about concurrency, connection-pool behaviour under load, or migration rollback; and the auth rows were seeded rather than produced by the auth library, so this exercises the profile model on a real schema rather than a full sign-in path.

recommended.title: Contract module boundaries
recommended.acceptance: Shared vocabularies live in their own leaf modules, domain contracts live in one module each, index.ts is a re-export-only compatibility barrel rather than the authoritative public surface, and a wildcard exports map lets a new domain contract be added without touching package metadata or the barrel; no cycle-driven z.lazy remains and structural regressions prove the boundary rather than merely reflecting it; no schema behaviour changes

recommended.title: Playback-session candidate wire bounds match StreamCandidate bounds
recommended.acceptance: playbackSessionCandidateSchema uses THE SAME AUTHORITATIVE id and providerId limits as the StreamCandidate contract -- the exported MAX_STREAM_CANDIDATE_ID_CHARS and MAX_STREAM_CANDIDATE_PROVIDER_ID_CHARS -- and NOT copied numeric literals. PL-0708 exported those constants for exactly this reason; a copied literal would recreate the defect one layer out, which is the defect this task exists to close. Required: an oversized resolved candidate CANNOT RE-EXPAND ON THE SESSION WIRE after passing through another producer seam, which is the actual risk -- the contract bound governs what a provider may produce, and a second unbounded restatement downstream means the bound stops at the seam; fixture and Wikidata legitimate identifiers remain accepted, because a bound that rejects a real upstream id is an outage rather than a fix; tests cover the EXACT MAXIMUM, MAXIMUM PLUS ONE, and the serialized response, since a bound tested only from above does not prove the boundary is where it is claimed to be; reason and error output does not echo the oversized value; and NO SECOND INDEPENDENT BOUND VOCABULARY IS INTRODUCED. Note while working: playbackSessionCandidateSchema also carries unbounded uri and mimeType. They are not named in the reviewer's acceptance and are not in scope by default -- if they warrant bounds, say so and let the reviewer rule rather than adding them quietly.
